title: Checking for understanding during a lesson
subject: Teacher training
objectives: Explain why asking 'Does everyone understand?' does not tell you who understood.
Use three quick checks that show every child's answer.
Decide what to do next from what the checks show.

blocks.text: Children who are lost often stay quiet. If we only find out at the end of the week, they have fallen further behind. A quick check in the middle of a lesson tells us who needs help while there is still time to give it.
Asking 'Does everyone understand?' rarely works. Most children say yes, even when they do not understand, because they do not want to stand out.

blocks.definition: Every child writes the answer on a slate or paper and holds it up at the same time.
Children show 1, 2, 3 or 4 fingers to pick one of four answers you have written on the board.
One short question every child answers on paper before the lesson ends.

blocks.title: In a Grade 4 maths class
blocks.text: The teacher writes 3/4 and 2/4 on the board and asks which is bigger. On 'Show me', 30 slates go up. She sees that 8 children wrote 2/4, so she works with those 8 for five minutes while the others do two more questions.

sections.title: What to do with what you see

items: Look at all the answers before you say anything.
If most children are right, move on and help the few at their seats.
If many are wrong, teach the idea again in a different way.
Note which children were wrong, and check them again tomorrow.
Do not praise or blame individual answers in front of the class.
Keep checks short: one or two minutes.
Use them at least twice in every lesson.

questions.prompt: If the class answers 'yes' to 'Does everyone understand?', you can move on safely.
questions.explanation: Children often say yes when they are lost. A check that shows every child's answer tells you much more.

questions.prompt: Which check shows every child's answer at the same moment?
questions.explanation: With Show me, all slates go up together, so you see every answer.

questions.prompt: Most of the class got the check wrong. What should you do?
choices: Move on to the next topic
Teach the idea again in a different way
questions.explanation: When many are wrong, the first explanation did not work for them. Try another way.

questions.prompt: Name the check children answer on paper before the lesson ends.
questions.explanation: An exit question gives you one answer from every child to plan the next lesson.

terms.definition: Finding out during a lesson which children have learned the idea and which have not.
Every child holds up a written answer at the same time.
A short question every child answers before leaving the lesson.

summary: Check during the lesson, not only at the end. Use checks that show every child's answer, such as Show me, fingers and an exit question. Look at all the answers, then move on, re-teach or help a small group.
